# Independent Gamma source-chain integration review

The current adapter, complete builder, shared Markdown preparation path, saved layout receipt and both complete script diffs were read directly. The stored source representations were then compared independently without executing the adapter, builder, Pandoc, compiler, or any mathematical regression checker. All 33 source/layout comparisons pass. No file under the cumulative reader root or any frozen edition was modified by this review.

The adapter's source is the complete delivered `RESEARCH_NOTE.md`, not the alternate `NOTE.tex`. The actual generated path is `build/source_gamma_convolution.tex`; there is no `tex/source_gamma_convolution.tex`. The current source receipt and the actual appendix wrapper both select that build path.

## Exact editions inspected

All reader-relative paths in this report refer to `output/split_zero_rh_tandem_2026-09-12` in the math workspace. The machine-readable companion contains the byte length and SHA256 of every inspected input, plus all 223 individual math-node hashes.

The layout revision directory is `work/gamma_reader_proposed_20260913/layout_revision_03`. The two current scripts were compared with its before snapshots by reconstructing their complete unified diffs. Those reconstructed diffs agree exactly with the saved diff files. Thus the adapter change adds only the new layout function; the builder change adds only the three-line Gamma-specific import and call after Markdown preparation. No other script delta is hidden by this comparison.

## Complete adapter and builder path

`GAMMA_MARKDOWN_SPEC` pins the exact original source path, SHA256, byte length, provenance path, complete-source attribution, and zero Lean source blocks. Its revision is explicitly the source SHA rather than an invented repository commit. The complete shared `prepare_pasted_witness` implementation verifies source length/hash/provenance before writing prepared Markdown, compares the original and prepared code-block lists, converts to TeX, adjusts generated navigation labels and breakable code typography, and returns the wrapper and receipt row. These are presentation operations on generated files. For the present Gamma source, the prepared Markdown is actually byte-identical to the original complete Markdown.

The builder iterates the exact imported `GAMMA_MARKDOWN_SPEC` object alongside its other complete Markdown witnesses. Immediately after `prepare_pasted_witness` returns, it tests `witness is GAMMA_MARKDOWN_SPEC` and calls the new function only for that object. The function resolves `builder.ROOT / row['converted']`; in the current actual row this is `build/source_gamma_convolution.tex`. Its sole file write is to that generated TeX path. The original Markdown, alternate complete TeX, and frozen editions are not write targets of this function.

The function requires exactly one occurrence of the complete original display before replacement. The original display literal was extracted as inert Python AST data for this review; the adapter was not imported or invoked. This exact-match requirement is material: the inverse is proved for this pinned display, whose text has no pre-existing alignment ampersands, aligned wrapper, or double-backslash row break. The adapter's broad string replacements are not asserted to be a universal inverse for arbitrary LaTeX mathematics.

The generated appendix wrapper has precisely one `\input{build/source_gamma_convolution.tex}`. The current build receipt's Gamma source row equals the actual current `source_receipt.json` row, including the two display hashes and its declared layout operation.

## Exact inverse of the actual five-line display

The original display, including its final punctuation, is:

```tex
\[
\text{original split-supported polynomial source}
\longrightarrow\text{full gamma product fibre with arithmetic amplitude}
\longrightarrow\text{sum density and retained relative component}
\longrightarrow\text{exact all-tensor arithmetic coefficients}
\longrightarrow\text{the same source--boundary Toda determinant ratio}.
\]
```

Its SHA256 as the exact UTF-8 display string is `d48e8fd0b396b343901d4eef27ac7abcd69b6c28b281245efc4b47aa791d8805`. The actual generated display is:

```tex
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\text{original split-supported polynomial source}\\
&\longrightarrow\text{full gamma product fibre with arithmetic amplitude}\\
&\longrightarrow\text{sum density and retained relative component}\\
&\longrightarrow\text{exact all-tensor arithmetic coefficients}\\
&\longrightarrow\text{the same source--boundary Toda determinant ratio}.
\end{aligned}
\]
```

Its SHA256 is `28153a8231ff5c7fe1eab5be9eec29682c53989a48072844ab1455ec090c1dc7`. Both hashes agree with the current source receipt.

The independent inverse operates on the actual generated display, rather than merely recreating what the adapter is intended to write. It first requires the exact outer `aligned` wrapper and exactly five content rows. It requires one leading ampersand on each row and exactly five ampersands in the block. The first four rows must terminate with the exact two-backslash row-break marker; the last row must not have that marker. It removes only those five initial alignment markers, four terminal row-break markers, and two outer alignment lines. The original `\[` and `\]` remain.

The result equals the complete original display string exactly. No whitespace stripping, token simplification, symbol replacement, polynomial normalization, or reordering is used. In particular all four `\longrightarrow` tokens, all five `\text{...}` payloads, their order, the double hyphen in `source--boundary`, and the final period remain unchanged.

Replacing that single actual block by the reconstructed original block also recovers the entire saved pre-layout generated source. This was checked both as full decoded text and as complete file bytes with the actual line-ending representation retained. Thus no generated material outside this one display was changed by the layout repair.

## All 223 mathematical nodes

The original and prepared stored Pandoc JSON files are byte-identical. Traversing their actual `Math` nodes yields exactly 223 ordered nodes: 60 `DisplayMath` and 163 `InlineMath`. Their ordered type-and-payload lists agree strictly.

Independently extracting every `\[...\]` and `\(...\)` math span from the alternate original `NOTE.tex` gives the same 223 ordered nodes. Each complete payload equals its corresponding original Pandoc payload character for character, including its existing leading/trailing newlines. No trimming or whitespace mapping is required in this comparison.

The current generated TeX also has exactly 223 nodes with the same type distribution. Before reversing the layout, 222 ordered nodes already agree exactly with the original. The only difference is node **221**, the source's final five-object chain. After applying the exact inverse above to that one block, all 223 generated nodes agree strictly in type and complete payload with both the original Pandoc nodes and alternate original `NOTE.tex` spans. The companion JSON records every index, node type, exact payload hash, and equality result.

The current source receipt's `inline_math_spans: 0` has a narrower mechanical scope: that shared preliminary regex counts backslash-parenthesis inline math in the Markdown source, whose actual inline math uses dollar delimiters. It is not the total inline count. This review independently establishes the total of 163 inline nodes from the complete stored Pandoc trees and both TeX representations. The source receipt's 60 displayed spans, zero punctuation protections, and unchanged prepared source are consistent with the inspected implementation.

## Receipt scope and result

The saved `layout_revision_03/RECEIPT.json` says `build_succeeded: false`. That is its historical repair state; it must not be quoted as successful compilation evidence. The current `build/build_receipt.json` separately records `status: compiled`, 478 pages, and PDF SHA256 `9e79bd6cb4f95d845af0f637a1cb4fdcb56ddf32015f89430fa12c530b8b1680`. This review reads that receipt to identify the integrated source row and edition. It does not claim an independent PDF render, visual inspection, or compilation.

The saved receipt also reports that five authored proofs, raw sources, and eighteen inherited appendices were unchanged. The coordinating source audit owns the full plan, fragment, inherited-appendix, conclusion, and main-file comparisons. This report proves the exact current Gamma Markdown and alternate TeX pins, complete original/prepared Markdown and Pandoc identity, complete current script diffs, exact one-block layout inverse, complete pre-layout generated-byte reconstruction, and every mathematical-node equality. It does not promote the remaining inherited-file booleans into checks it did not perform.

The read-only verification program is `work/gamma_chain_integration_review_20260913.py`; it writes only `work/gamma_chain_integration_review_20260913.json`. Its completed execution returned zero with all 33 comparisons passing. All inspected input hashes were taken again at the end and remained unchanged. The companion JSON SHA256 is `399cd528041daf486b18e0d9c2532034856aeaf937a0e64aa352dd5d15a9ca6f`.

No unresolved content or mathematical-token defect was found in this integration change. The complete five-object chain and all other original mathematics are retained exactly under the documented presentation map.
